---
title: "Assignment 4 — Phonons and harmonic thermodynamics"
---

Laboratory 4 connects two subjects that may initially appear separate:

- vibrational frequencies and spectroscopy;
- thermodynamic properties of a crystalline solid.

The connection is made by **phonons**. A vibrational calculation tells us which
quantized lattice excitations are available. Statistical thermodynamics tells
us how those excitations are populated as temperature changes.

The central numerical question of the laboratory is:

> **How much of the first Brillouin zone must be sampled before the harmonic
> thermodynamic properties of MgO are numerically converged?**

## What you will calculate

You will calculate two phonon datasets yourself:

1. the primitive-cell frequencies at $\Gamma$;
2. a $2\times2\times2$ `SCELPHONO` calculation.

Validated $3\times3\times3$ and $4\times4\times4$ datasets will be supplied by
the instructor. They are deliberately provided because their computational
cost is not the learning objective of this course.

All calculations use:

- the optimized MgO geometry from Laboratory 3;
- the SHRINK value that you selected in Laboratory 2;
- the same DFT functional, basis set and numerical thresholds used previously.

## What you will compare

For each sampling level, Quantas will be used to calculate harmonic
thermodynamic properties. The main comparison will be the heat capacity:

```text
Γ only
2×2×2
3×3×3
4×4×4
experimental data
```

The objective is to separate two different issues:

1. **q-point convergence** — a numerical sampling problem;
2. **remaining disagreement with experiment** — a limitation of the physical
   model and its approximations.

Your answers are written directly in the notebooks.
